summary: Ships apart from two small gaps: since is never tested together with page/pageSize, and the numeric-id assumption is undocumented. F1-F3 are fixed at the root. npm test passes 8/8 and lint is clean. Opened src/server.mjs, src/store.mjs, test/notes.test.mjs, test/helpers.mjs, src/client.mjs, AGENTS.md and package.json, and grepped for since/.list( callers: store.list's only caller is server.mjs, and client.mjs never sends since, so no caller is broken and the response shape is unchanged.

findings.issue: F4 is still open. No test combines since with page/pageSize. The code filters by since before slicing the page, and total counts only the filtered notes, but no test checks either. A later change that slices first and filters second would pass every current test. Nothing guards the documented paging contract (items/total/page/pageSize) when since is set.
findings.fix: Add a test: alice adds a1..a5, bob adds b1, then GET /notes?since=<a1.id>&page=2&pageSize=2. Assert items are ['a4','a5'] and total is 4.

findings.code: // page is 1-based. since: only notes created after the note with that id.
findings.issue: F5 is still open. since assumes ids are numeric and increase with creation time (Number(n.id) > since), but outside callers only see string ids. The contract is not documented in AGENTS.md, and neither the client nor a README mentions since. If the id scheme ever changes (UUIDs, for example), Number(n.id) becomes NaN, NaN > since is false, and a since query silently returns nothing.
findings.fix: Document the since contract (a numeric note id, exclusive, needs sequential numeric ids) in AGENTS.md or a README, or next to the /notes route in server.mjs. Optionally add a since option to client.mjs so it stays in step with the server.

pre_existing.issue: A malformed page or pageSize (for example page=abc or pageSize=-5) silently falls back to the default instead of returning a 4xx. That is inconsistent with the new since validation, which returns 400. There is also no upper bound on pageSize.
all() makes one sequential request per page (a round trip for every 50 notes). This is untouched by the diff.
